task_message:
Case L05: segment the lipomatous soft-tissue tumor on this T1-weighted MRI.

Volume: 261x261x211 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.
final_assistant_text:
The case is complete. 

**Summary of what I did for case L05 (lipomatous soft-tissue tumor, T1 MRI):**

1. **Orientation** — `seg_open` plus axial/coronal/sagittal contact sheets showed a large fat-signal (T1-hyperintense), septated mass occupying the anterior/lateral compartment of the thigh, deep to the fascia, adjacent to the femur and displacing the quadriceps.
2. **Initial segmentation** — a point prompt gave a conservative 115 mL blob; I zoomed in, generated edge marks on the slice of maximum cross-section and used a lasso to make the contour follow the true capsule (v2, 141 mL).
3. **Correcting under-coverage** — slice-by-slice inspection (axial 50–62, 135–210) showed the lesion continued much further distally (a tapering tail down to ~axial 200) and proximally, so I added positive points at axial 175 inside the missed lobule (v3, 310 mL, axial 47–202, one single connected component).
4. **Verification** — three-plane overlay checks plus the automatic candidates: C1–C3 corresponded to the bright subcutaneous fat ring and intermuscular fat (normal tissue), and the past-the-mask review panels (axial 210, coronal 202, sagittal 137) contained no lesion tissue, so no candidates were accepted.

**Final mask:** v3, 310.3 mL, single component, spanning axial 47–202, coronal 117–194, sagittal 57–129, saved with medium confidence (the lesion–fat contrast is subtle at the tapering tips).
